problem: For integers r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1 let P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q * [b]_{q^r}, where [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} and [b]_{q^r} = 1+q^r+...+q^{r(b-1)}. P is (weakly) unimodal if its coefficients satisfy c_0<=...<=c_m>=...>=c_N for some m. U = {b : P unimodal}, F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1). Question: exactly which parameters make P unimodal? (Source: arXiv:2605.12822, Conjecture 5.4.)

claims.statement: (Thread criterion) P_b unimodal iff for every thread V_b>=0 and V_{b-1}+d_b>=0, with the parity split; S2(i): b in U and b == F (mod 2) => b+1 in U, hence max U == 1+F (mod 2) when r divides no a_i; step-2 closure: b in U, b>=3 => b-2 in U; Theorem 15: U finite iff r divides no a_i; Theorem 17 (conditional S2).

Theorem R: S2 follows from three finite residue-level conditions (TP_rho, E_rho, O_rho) on the small-part instance rho = residues; Lemma 10: b > B => not unimodal with B = 1+floor((2y*-D-1)/r), y* = least y with d_y<0.

Theorem 1: if r divides no a_i, U = [1,sigma] ∪ {sigma+2, sigma+4, ..., tau*-2} with sigma, tau* ≡ 1+F (mod 2), tau* >= sigma+2; corollaries S2(i), max U parity, closure under b->b-2, and S2 <=> tau* <= sigma+4. Includes Lemma 7 (cyclic unimodality of class sums).

Window Lemma (P unimodal iff tau_m + g_{K-m} - g_m >= 0 for the r integers m with K/2-r <= m < K/2); Sandwich theorem for all-equal a=nr+s with middle s (E(0)⊆E(1)⊆...; E(n)=E_inf for 2(nr+s) > k(s-1)+1-r); with computation C1 this proves U([nr+s]^k) = [1,kn+1] ∪ (kn+1+E_inf) for all n>=1, 4<=r<=30, 3<=k<=60; parity structure of E_inf (two chains, S2(i) for the family); closed form of tau.
